question.text: Twenty people were executed for being associated with the Devil during these series of hearings. Arthur Miller wrote about these events in The Crucible.
question.clue: Bridget Bishop was the first victim of this event, hanged after being accused of having a third nipple and tormenting five girls, including Abigail Williams.

swap.leadin: Name these New World Colonies now known by their state names.
swap.text: Captain John Smith helped to found Jamestown, a settlement within this colony.
swap.clue: A raid on Martin's Hundred by Opechancanough threatened this area.

question.text: Originally intended as a fort to protect the Dutch West India Company's fur interests in the area, this settlement was handed over to the British in exchange for a tiny island near Suriname in the Treaty of Breda. This settlement was later renamed New York City.
question.clue: A fort in this settlement was constructed by what became a non-Ohio Bowling Green.

swap.text: In this 1676 war, which included the Great Swamp Fight, a namesake chief fought soldiers and priests from Plymouth and Massachusetts Bay. Native or colonial name acceptable.
swap.answerHtml: King Philip’s War [or Metacomet’s War; or Pometacomet’s War; accept “rebellion” in place of “war”]
swap.clue: The display of Weetamoo's severed head in Taunton was related in a history of this war written by Increase Mather.

question.text: Ivar the Boneless conquered this city, which then became the center of the Danelaw. This city was the birthplace of the scholar Alcuin, who was the head of the palace school at Aachen.
question.clue: A scholar born in this city devised the first Western European script with lower-case letters and spacing between words and headed the palace school at Aachen.

swap.leadin: Everyone likes pirates! Answer these questions about real pirates.
swap.text: In 1718, this man blockaded the port of Charlestown with his ship The Queen Anne's Revenge and two smaller vessels. He allegedly lit fuses around his face to appear more menacing.
swap.clue: This man used the wealth gained from rogue toll operations in Pamlico Sound to purchase protection from Charles Eden of North Carolina and eventually redubbed the Concorde the Royal James after earlier flying it under the moniker Queen Anne's Revenge.

question.leadin: Answer the following about English-Native American relations in New England during the Colonial Period.
question.text: This Native American tribe is remembered by many as the tribe of Squanto which participated in the first Thanksgiving during the reign of chief Massasoit, although that has been debated.
question.clue: Three members of this tribe were tried and executed for the murder of John Sassamon, a "praying Indian."

swap.leadin: Identify these things about the English colonies in America.
swap.text: Pontiac's rebellion led to this British law forbidding colonists from moving past the Appalachian mountains because they were afraid of wars with Indians draining resources.
swap.clue: This law was modified within five years by the treaties of Hard Labor and Lochaber.

question.leadin: The temporary peace achieved under this man's leadership did not last under the rule of his brother Opechancanough (oh-pech-uh n-KAH-noh), who committed the Indian Massacre of 1622.
question.text: Name this Native American weroance, or chief, whose daughter possibly intervened at the last minute to save an Englishman from execution.
question.answerHtml: Powhatan [or Wahunsenacawh; or Powatan; or Pohetan; or Poughwaton; or Wahunsenasawk; or Wahunsenacock; or Wahunsenakah; accept Powhatan Confederacy; prompt on Mamanatowick]
question.clue: He was the high chief among the weorance and held the title of mamanatowick or "emperor" from his capital of Werowocomoco.

swap.leadin: This man was stabbed to death in 1769 by a member of the Peoria tribe.
swap.text: Name this chief of the Ottawa tribe and victor at the Battle of Bloody Run. Fort Pitt was besieged during a war named for this man.
swap.clue: A reward for this man's death was announced by Jeffrey Amherst.

question.leadin: The namesakes of this land survey were hired to settle a dispute between Maryland and Pennsylvania.
question.text: What pair of British astronomers created a namesake line that demarcates four states?
question.clue: They fulfilled the task by laying out a series of milestones bearing coats of arms until trouble with natives forced a return to Philadelphia.

swap.text: With the guidance of Guido Verbeck, Meiji commissioned one of these groups led by and named for Iwakura Tomomi. Another of these groups travelled to San Francisco aboard the western warship Kanrin Maru.
swap.clue: Examples of these structures, 21 of which were connected via a 600-mile path, included San Carlos Borromeo de Carmelo.

question.leadin: This tribe developed a voting procedure where a corn kernel meant agreement, while a pea meant opposition.
question.text: Name this matrilineal tribe that signed the Treaty of Middle Plantation with the English. This tribe's Queen Cockacoeske was succeeded by Queens Betty and Ann, who may have been the same person.
question.clue: This tribe's female chief Cockacoeske was killed during Bacon's Rebellion. Powhatan and his daughter Pocahontas belonged to this tribe.

swap.text: During the uprising, this group of drunken rangers massacred some unarmed Conestoga Indians in Pennsylvania.
swap.clue: Their first fight was prompted by Matthew Smith's reconnaissance, and Asher Clayton and Lazarus Stewart led their two companies, which were started by Colonel Reverend John Elder.

question.leadin: Robert Fogel posited one of these periods spanning roughly the 1960s through 80s, though William G. McLoughlin's thesis about the third period of this type is much more widely accepted.
question.text: Name these periods of spiritual revival in America, whose first iteration was exemplified by Jonathan Edwards and George Whitefield.
question.answerHtml: Great Awakenings [accept First, Second, Third, or Fourth Great Awakening]
question.clue: In 1801, over 20,000 people participated in one of these events by attending the Cane Ridge Revival in Kentucky.

swap.text: James Alexander used the pseudonym Cato in essays published by an editor of this ethnicity who was accused of libel in 1733. The first Speaker of the House was of this ethnicity.
swap.clue: Immigrants of this ethnicity practiced gymnastics in clubs called Turner Halls.

question.text: This President of Harvard spoke out against the Salem witch trials in Cases of Conscience Concerning Evil Spirits. He also penned An Essay for the Recording of Illustrious Provinces, and attacked Edmund Andros in A Narrative of the Miseries of New England.
question.clue: This man became president of Harvard in 1685 and served in that position until 1701.

swap.leadin: This association created a five-member court to run its territory chaired by John Carter, and negotiated with Cherokee Indians to make the Transylvania Purchase.
swap.text: Name this association which, in 1772, established an autonomous republic on the banks of the namesake river in Tennessee when they realized they were living south of the official territory of North Carolina.

question.leadin: This person called on God to "wrest America out of the Hands of its old Land-Lord, Satan" in The Present State of New England.
question.text: Name this Puritan minister and proponent of smallpox inoculation, the son of another minister named Increase.
question.clue: A bomb was thrown through this man's window with a note attached reading "I'll inoculate you with this" after this man's slave, Onesimus, taught him about variolation and he encouraged its adoption during a smallpox epidemic.

swap.text: This Massachusetts Bay Colony leader, who story is told by Edmund Morgan in The Puritan Dilemma, booted Williams out for his agitation, which led Williams to go found Rhode Island.
swap.clue: He sided with Thomas Dudley and John Endecott in a dispute that led to the banishment of John Wheelwright.
